title: Fail-Closed Alignment for Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2602.16977v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We identify a structural weakness in current large language model (LLM) alignment: refusal mechanisms in these models are fail-open. While existing approaches tend to encode refusal behaviors across multiple latent features, suppressing a single feature (via prompt-based jailbreaks) is sufficient to collapse alignment, leading to unsafe generation. Motivated by this, we propose fail-closed alignment as a design principle for robust LLM safety: refusal mechanisms should remain effective even under partial failures via redundant, independent causal pathways. We present a concrete instantiation of this principle: a progressive alignment framework that iteratively identifies and ablates previously learned refusal directions, forcing the model to reconstruct safety along new, independent subspaces. Across six jailbreak attacks, our method achieves the lowest observed average attack success rate (1.6%) while largely preserving generation q

translated_title: 大语言模型的失效关闭对齐
translated_abstract: 我们发现了当前大语言模型（LLM）对齐中的一个结构性弱点：这些模型的拒绝机制是“失效开放”的。现有方法倾向于将拒绝行为编码在多个潜在特征中，然而只需抑制单个特征（通过基于提示词的越狱攻击）就足以使对齐崩溃，导致不安全的生成内容。受此启发，我们提出“失效关闭”对齐作为鲁棒LLM安全的设计原则：即使发生部分故障，拒绝机制也应通过冗余且独立的因果路径保持有效。我们给出了该原则的一个具体实例：一个渐进式对齐框架，它迭代地识别并消融先前学到的拒绝方向，迫使模型在新的、独立的子空间中重构安全性。在六种越狱攻击下，我们的方法实现了最低的平均攻击成功率（1.6%），同时基本保持了生成质量。
tldr: 提出失效关闭对齐设计原则及渐进式对齐框架，通过迭代消融已学到的拒绝方向、迫使模型在独立子空间中重构安全性，将越狱攻击平均成功率降至1.6%。
